content_voiceover: This page reviews two exam questions on acute myeloid leukemia therapy. The first asks about frontline AML treatment, and the correct answer is none of the above. Venetoclax plus azacitidine works across FLT3 and IDH mutated AML regardless of whether midostaurin, ivosidenib, or enasidenib were given, so those pairing statements are false. Oral azacitidine, from the QUAZAR AML-001 trial, prolongs overall survival as maintenance in older patients who achieved remission with induction chemotherapy but were not going on to transplant, so tying its benefit to patients who also received allogeneic transplant is incorrect. And sorafenib maintenance after transplant, from the SORMAIN trial, showed a relapse free survival benefit for FLT3 ITD AML, not a clearly proven overall survival benefit. The second question asks which statement about therapy related AML is wrong, and it's the one describing latency. Alkylating agent related AML has the longer latency, around five to ten years, while topoisomerase two inhibitor related AML develops much sooner, typically within one to three years. This question reversed those latencies.
keypoints: Venetoclax azacitidine benefits FLT3 and IDH mutated AML independent of prior targeted therapy
QUAZAR trial: oral azacitidine maintenance improves survival mainly in patients not proceeding to transplant
SORMAIN trial: sorafenib after transplant improves relapse free survival, not proven overall survival
Topoisomerase two inhibitor related AML has a short latency, one to three years
Alkylating agent related AML has a longer latency, five to ten years
keypoint_voiceover: Remember, venetoclax based regimens work across FLT3 and IDH mutated AML no matter what targeted therapy came before. The QUAZAR trial's survival benefit for oral azacitidine maintenance applies to patients who did not go to transplant. SORMAIN showed sorafenib maintenance improves relapse free survival after transplant, but overall survival benefit is not firmly established. And don't mix up the latencies, alkylating agents take longer to cause secondary AML than topoisomerase two inhibitors do.
